objections.claim: The product needs to integrate with the CRM because reps won't use a separate tab.
objections.quote: It's got to land in the CRM. My reps aren't going to go looking for another tab, they just won't.

objections.claim: The lack of a current HubSpot integration is a significant gap.
objections.quote: That's a real gap for us.

objections.claim: The prospect has concerns regarding the pricing.
objections.quote: And the other thing's the number, obviously. I did look at the pricing page.

intent.claim: The prospect is interested in moving forward but requires a CRM integration date and financial approval.
intent.quote: It's not a no, but I'd want a date.

nextSteps.claim: Prospect will check Dave's calendar and send an invite for Thursday or Friday.
nextSteps.quote: Thursday or Friday, I'll check his calendar and send an invite.

nextSteps.claim: Rep will prepare a one-page document for the meeting with Dave.
nextSteps.quote: I'll have the page ready either way.

sections.summary: The prospect is interested in moving forward but raised objections regarding pricing and the lack of a HubSpot integration, stating that the product must integrate with their CRM for representative adoption. Next steps include the prospect sending a calendar invite for Thursday or Friday to meet with Dave, and the representative preparing a one-page document for that meeting. Final approval is contingent on financial sign-off and a confirmed integration date.
sections.followUpEmail:
Thank you for the conversation. We discussed the necessity of a CRM integration to ensure rep adoption and noted that the current lack of a HubSpot integration is a significant gap. We also touched upon concerns regarding the pricing. While there is interest in moving forward, this is contingent upon receiving a date for the CRM integration and obtaining financial approval.

As agreed, I will prepare a one-page document for the upcoming meeting. I look forward to receiving the calendar invite for Thursday or Friday.
